description:
Five stacked entry functions run a plan against operands in the interpreter: select_clause (src/ir_interp/backend.rs:704), select_dispatch_body (:790, one .map over twelve lines of signature), select_dispatch_match (:959), execute_dispatch_inputs (dispatch_exec.rs:74, one field read), execute_dispatch_node (:88, the walk). select_dispatch_match hides DispatchOperands from its callers, so backend.rs:1344-1348 and :1462-1466 rebuild identical operands right after it returns, per case and per receive attempt. select_clause allocates vec![Absent; n] and clones a lane vector per required input (:714-721) although args is already &[Option<BackendBoundValue>] and Absent is None.

Change: delete execute_dispatch_inputs and select_dispatch_body; select_dispatch_match takes &DispatchOperands, built once per call and reused for the outcome arguments; select_clause borrows its argument slice. An omitted required input is still an error, tested the same way.

Signal: the case, receive and entry fixture lanes on three doors; a mis-threaded state surfaces as "winning outcome lacks subject". Concept that stops existing: two signature adapters, operands built twice, copying arguments in order to dispatch on them.
title: One door into the interpreter's dispatch; arguments are borrowed, not copied
